A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Panda research project. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on synthetic ODEs, experimental time series and PDEs, together with architectural ablations, diversity scaling and masked-completion results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds dataset diagnostics, distributional evaluations, patch-length ablations, larger-model comparisons and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The core patch embedding, temporal/channel attention, prediction heads and objectives remain. However, v1 names NoPE while v2 specifies p-RoPE, and v2 newly describes KPSS/ADF stationarity filtering. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent procedural changes or corrected and expanded implementation documentation.

E1.justification: Both cover chaotic ODE forecasting and completion, double-pendulum motion, eigenworms, electronic circuits, and KS/VKVS PDE forecasting. The enlarged training datasets vary system counts, initial conditions and integration timescales within retained coverage. Some founder-system examples separately identified in v2 were already plotted in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds Chronos 200M comparisons in Appendix D and Chronos 46M, including supervised-fine-tuned and probabilistic variants, in Appendix K. This extends the existing Chronos comparator family; the original main comparison set remains. Time-MoE is excluded from the new significance tests because of NaNs, but remains in benchmark plots.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported Chronos-SFT budget from 300K iterations to ten times Panda's iterations; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include distributional evaluation over four contexts per system, patch-length comparisons with embedding removal and batch-size adjustments, and 42M/72M models with larger datasets and training budgets. The reported founder-pool size also changes from 135 to 129.

E4.justification: v2 adds dataset-diversity and chaoticity diagnostics, forecast-distribution and Lyapunov analyses, patch-length sensitivity, model/data scaling studies, and explicit comparative failure cases. These test substantial new questions about dataset quality, generalization and forecast validity. The original architectural ablations and attention analyses remain, with attention analysis relocated to Appendix G.

E5.justification: v2 adds Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Sidak adjustment in Table 5, plus mean-and-standard-deviation summaries for distributional and timing analyses. Existing median/IQR reporting, PDE standard-error bars and five-mask completion averaging were already present. These additions do not establish increased independent training repetitions.

E6.justification: Substantial new numerical and qualitative results appear. At horizon 128, Table 1 reports KL divergence of 1.18 for Panda versus 1.72 for Chronos-SFT probabilistic; Table 17 reports sMAPE 20.6 for the new 72M Panda. Prediction-only Lyapunov comparisons also reveal advantages for Chronos-SFT. The enlarged-model results use different training conditions and are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces an explicit empirical stiffness-score definition using the logarithm of the maximum-to-average finite-difference ratio. The skew-product equations receive fuller exposition, while the correlation-dimension estimator and linear-attention coupling derivation are substantively retained. No substantial new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract adds preservation of long-term statistics as a central forecasting claim, replacing nonlinear resonance as a highlighted emergent property. The introduction also revises its claimed real-world applications, replacing chemical-reaction/electrophysiology examples with the evaluated motion and circuit applications. Zero-shot PDE forecasting and dynamical-diversity scaling claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix M newly acknowledge Panda's regression to the mean beyond its training horizon and contrast this with Chronos parroting and geometric failures. v2 also interprets dataset diagnostics as evidence against diversity collapse and qualifies optimal patch length as data-dependent. Most earlier attention-based mechanism explanations are retained in the appendix.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the Radau integration procedure, period selection, optimizer and learning-rate schedule, clipping, augmentation frequency, expanded architecture settings and training budgets. It newly documents PDE initialization and PCA-based vorticity inputs. Dataset/checkpoint links are added, the code repository target changes, and the reported training node changes from four to eight GPUs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting stationarity tests, skew-product flows and distributional evaluation, including Dickey-Fuller, Kwiatkowski et al., Kloeden-Kozyakin and Hess et al. It removes the conserved-quantities related-work paragraph and several resonance analogies and associated citations. The principal positioning against synthetic-data and PDE foundation models remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, dataset procedure and architecture exposition undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. The main narrative replaces the attention-analysis section with long-term geometry evaluation, relocating retained attention material and reorganizing the appendices. The title, terminology and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds extensive distributional, statistical, ablation and scaling tables, together with diagnostic and failure-analysis figures. Forecast example grids are regrouped, and the main attention/resonance figures move to Appendix G. Core benchmark plots are retained, while headings, title formatting and page layout are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked quantitative forecast-distribution validation and several essential replication settings. v2 supplies these, adds dataset-quality checks and adjusted significance tests, and documents comparative failures, substantially strengthening evidential support and reproducibility. Important limits remain: scale-up changes data and budgets together, while mean regression and mixed prediction-only Lyapunov results qualify the stronger long-term preservation claim.
